answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation: every agent identity must lock a deposit before it can transact. Reputation accrues like a glacier — slow, layered, hard to fake — while new identities wander with low trust until they prove themselves. The river of Sybil pressure is drained by economics: an attacker needs one deposit per fake identity plus fees per transaction, so a thousand fakes costs a thousand deposits. Misbehavior slashes the bond and taints the linked identity cluster, making the attackers cost scale linearly with each Sybil while honest agents pay only once.
